Name: ElementBlades
Author: Herolin0027
Description:
[b][size=5]Element Blades [/size][/b]
Element Blades adds four powerful, forgeable, and enchantable elemental swords to Stardew Valley. Charge your weapon through normal attacks, then release a large flying crescent with knockback, shockwave, burning, or freezing effects.
[heading]Four Elemental Blades[/heading]
[b]Windfeather Blade[/b]
A fast and lightweight sword. Its crescent travels up to 15 tiles and has strong knockback.
[b]Tempest Blade[/b]
A broad, heavy sword. Its first projectile hit creates a large shockwave that damages nearby monsters.
[b]Flame Blade[/b]
Applies a six-second burning effect. Repeated hits refresh the duration instead of stacking multiple burns.
[b]Frost Blade[/b]
Freezes ordinary monsters. Special or modded monsters generally receive a movement slowdown instead.
All four swords support vanilla gemstone forging and combat enchantments. Galaxy Souls are not required. These are intentionally powerful late-game weapons, with fully Ruby-forged melee damage exceeding an equally forged Infinity Blade.
[heading]Controls[/heading]
[list]
[*]Swing three times to fully charge the equipped blade. Swings into empty space also count.[/*]
[*]The fourth swing releases an elemental crescent.[/*]
[*]Using the normal sword block immediately fills the charge, while preserving the original defensive action.[/*]
[*]Keyboard and controller inputs use the game’s normal bindings.[/*]
[*]Charge indicators appear beside the equipped weapon icon on the toolbar.[/*]
[/list]Projectiles pierce monsters and, by default, walls. Range and map boundaries still apply. Each projectile can directly damage a monster only once.
Flying blades can break mine crates and barrels while preserving their normal drops. Player storage chests, machines, crops, and ore are not destroyed.
[heading]Weapon Acquisition[/heading]
The four blades become available from the Adventurer’s Guild after reaching mine floor 40. Each sword costs 75,000g.
The unlock floor, purchase price, damage, speed, projectile range, crescent width, and elemental effects can all be changed through the configuration file.
Lowering the unlock requirement does not automatically reduce the weapons’ power.
[heading]Sound and Configuration[/heading]
Generic Mod Config Menu is supported but optional.
Each player can independently control:
[list]
[*]All additional weapon sounds[/*]
[*]Charge-ready sounds[/*]
[*]Projectile-release sounds[/*]
[*]Tempest shockwave sounds[/*]
[/list]Sound preferences are stored separately for each save and player. These settings affect the mod’s additional audio cues and do not disable vanilla attack or hit sounds.
Split-screen players share the same physical audio output, so sounds enabled by another local player may still be heard.
Without Generic Mod Config Menu, close the game and edit
[code]config.json[/code].
[heading]Multiplayer[/heading]
All multiplayer participants should install the same mod version and use matching combat and shop settings.
Elemental damage and status effects are resolved by the host. Personal sound preferences can be configured independently.
Direct projectile kills, Flame burn kills, and Tempest shockwave kills count toward the actual attacker’s personal monster-slay quests, including online farmhands and local split-screen players.
[heading]Installation[/heading]
[list=1]
[*]Install SMAPI.[/*]
[*]Close the game.[/*]
[*]Download and extract the archive.[/*]
[*]Place the included
[code]ElementBlades[/code]folder inside your Stardew Valley
[code]Mods[/code]directory.[/*]
[*]Launch the game through SMAPI.[/*]
[/list]The correct installation path is:
[code]Mods/ElementBlades/manifest.json[/code]When upgrading from the old WindBlade release, back up your save and configuration, remove the old
[code]Mods/WindBlade[/code]folder, and then install Element Blades.
Existing weapon IDs are retained for save compatibility, so previously obtained weapons, forging, enchantments, and charge data should remain recognized.
[heading]Requirements[/heading]
[list]
[*]Stardew Valley 1.6[/*]
[*]SMAPI 4.0 or later[/*]
[*]Generic Mod Config Menu — optional[/*]
[*]Content Patcher is not required[/*]
[/list]English and Chinese weapon text and player guides are included. Some configuration menu labels and console messages may still appear in Chinese.
[heading]Compatibility and Support[/heading]
The mod has passed compilation, automated combat and configuration tests, and integration checks against the Windows Stardew Valley 1.6.15 game assemblies.
More live multiplayer, split-screen, platform, and combat-mod compatibility testing is still welcome.
When reporting an issue, please include:
[list]
[*]Your SMAPI log[/*]
[*]Mod version[/*]
[*]Single-player, online multiplayer, or split-screen mode[/*]
[*]The affected weapon[/*]
[*]Clear reproduction steps[/*]
[/list][heading]Uninstallation[/heading]
Back up your save first. Remove all Element Blades weapons from player inventories and storage, save and exit the game, then delete the
[code]Mods/ElementBlades[/code]folder.
Created by [b]Herolin0027[/b].
Gallery images are asset previews and are not gameplay screenshots.

Downloads.Description: Recommended version. Adds per-player master, charge, release and impact sound controls. Fixes monster-slay quest credit for projectile, burn and shockwave kills in multiplayer and split-screen. Requires Stardew Valley 1.6 and SMAPI 4.0+.
